rules.action: Intravascular imaging (IVUS or OCT) recommended for complex PCI.
rules.rationale: Class IA recommendation supported by RENOVATE-COMPLEX-PCI and OCTOBER — upgraded from prior IIa. Imaging-guided PCI reduces MACE in anatomically complex lesions.
rules.detail: Pre-stent imaging guides sizing and preparation. Post-stent imaging confirms expansion, apposition, and identifies edge dissection before completing.

rules.action: IVUS mandatory for LM PCI. MSA targets: LM ≥8mm², LAD ostium ≥6mm², LCx ostium ≥5mm².
rules.rationale: IVUS-guided LM PCI reduces MACE. MSA targets are the minimum acceptable — do not complete without achieving them.
rules.detail: If MSA target is not met, post-dilate with an appropriately sized NC balloon before completing.

rules.action: IVUS mandatory at multiple time points: pre-stenting for sizing, post-stenting for MSA confirmation.
rules.rationale: LM bifurcation has the highest risk of inadequate stent result — MSA optimisation is directly associated with outcomes.
rules.detail: MSA targets: LM ≥8mm², LAD ostium ≥6mm², LCx ostium ≥5mm². Post-dilate if any target is unmet.

rules.action: IVUS strongly recommended for proximal LAD PCI.
rules.rationale: Large territory at risk makes stent underexpansion and edge dissection particularly consequential. MSA optimisation reduces MACE.
rules.detail: OCT is an acceptable alternative where detailed plaque characterisation is needed.

rules.action: IVUS recommended for ostial lesions — angiographic positioning at the ostium is unreliable.
rules.rationale: IVUS confirms accurate landing zone, prevents stent protrusion into the parent vessel, and guides post-dilatation with balloon flaring.

rules.action: Post-stent intravascular imaging recommended to confirm SB ostial coverage, MV expansion, and absence of proximal edge dissection.
rules.rationale: Post-stent imaging changes management in a significant proportion of bifurcation cases.
rules.detail: IVUS preferred for LM bifurcations. OCT acceptable for non-LM bifurcations.

rules.action: Intravascular imaging most useful for confirming stent expansion in large grafts and identifying significant under-expansion.
rules.rationale: Large graft diameter and eccentric degenerated plaque can make angiographic sizing unreliable.
rules.detail: Routine imaging is not mandated for all SVG PCI but should be considered when stent sizing is uncertain. IVUS interpretation can be challenging in very degenerated grafts.
